title: Demand Service Rate Programs: Working Out the Figure That Clears a Demand Service Account
content:
## The clause

The figure that clears the demand service account is worked out from the charges standing on the rate
program, the payments already received on it, the credits set against it, what the program year's
emergency dispatches owe and any allowance for settling. The ledger window of this policy runs back 24
months from the day the account is settled. Only the charges that have fallen due within that ledger
window are taken in. No credit is set off. Nothing is taken in for emergency dispatches beyond the
year's included calls. The current program year runs from the day the current term started to the day
the account is settled. No allowance comes off. The figure is the charges taken in, less every payment
received on the program, less the credits set off, with the emergency dispatch element added and the
allowance taken off; the allowance is worked out on the charges taken in alone and never on the figure
after the payments and credits come off, and only the total is rounded, to the nearest cent, half up.

## The elements

| Element | What it stands at |
|---|---|
| the charges taken in | the charges invoiced on the rate program that have fallen due within the ledger window of 24 months |
| the payments | every payment received on the program, over its whole life and not over a window |
| the credits set off | nil |
| the emergency dispatch element | the dispatches counted against the current program year beyond the tier's included emergency calls, never fewer than none, multiplied by what is taken in for each such dispatch, nothing being taken in for them |
| the allowance | nil, worked out on the charges taken in alone |

The tier's included emergency calls are the figure published for the program the account holds under the
Demand Service Rate Programs.

## Worked through on a hypothetical ledger

A rate program whose charges falling due inside the ledger window total 9400 US dollars carries payments
of 6000 US dollars received over the life of the program. The charges taken in are 9400 US dollars, from
which the payments of 6000 US dollars come off, leaving 3400 US dollars; no credit is set off; the
emergency dispatch element is nil and the allowance is nil. Rounded to the nearest cent, half up, the
figure that clears the account is 3400.00 US dollars.
